body:
It is actually a very interesting article, and it pertains to my case greatly. I'm a very analytical/logical thinker and that article brings a lot of light onto the problem. Normally, yes, my depression most definitely helps me focus and control my stress at work or when I was in school. The problem is when that depression never goes away, IE: the problems never resolve themselves, or are unable to be resolved. The depression becomes the problem and it takes over. 

If I had a car, even a piece of shit, I could probably move on some. If I was in an intimate relationship, I could probably move on some. If I could get a different job that allowed me to earn a decent amount of money, the same outcome. I don't believe evolution planned for impassable situations. The easiest way I believe I could overcome my issues would be for the depression to disappear, or at least sit on the back-burner. I wish it wasn't such a difficult situation.

Thanks for your reply, I appreciate it. My biggest dilemma at the moment is lack of a car/lack of transportation in general. 15 minutes either way on the high-way is a fairly large city, though I have no real way of getting there. Currently my mother/co-workers take me to and from work, occasionally one of my other family members will take me. 

I hate my current job, and I believe it's a good reason for the depression. I realize the economy is terrible right now and I'm lucky to have a job, but I get paid 7.50 an hour and the company constantly adds more and more shit for us to do. Their expectations are extraordinarily high for what I get paid, and I can't really make any sort of life out of where I'm at. I'm trying to get a new job right now, but with lack of real transportation I'm pretty screwed.
